events.credibility_reason: Secondary sources attribute three conflicting omega bounds to the paper; original unread.
Algebra error at eq. 8 to eq. 9 identified in-thread; poster conceded.
2026 audit identifies an off-by-one error skipping 35 feasible exponents in the enumeration; no response from Zemann found.
Main theorem rests on a 79.75M-leaf enumeration with no public code or ledgers; claimed ledger independence overstated by the paper's own §5.8; authors have no other traceable publications.
events.ai_basis: AI systems (Anthropic's Claude, principally the Fable 5 and Opus model series, orchestrated in a multi-agent branch–synthesize–drill workflow with mandatory machine verification) carried out the computations, discovered and proved the lemmas, wrote and checked the Lean formalizations, ran the independent verification ledgers, and drafted the text.

events.credibility_reason: Claimed nonexistence of a long-open problem with no uptake in 16 months; both 2026 papers on the problem still call existence open; unidentified author; non-reviewing venue; content itself unreadable.

why: The statement asks only whether a quasiperfect number exists. Alekseyev's 10^45 result (25 Jan 2026, after the snapshot) is a finite search and so instances, as is the OEIS bound. The 2026 omega >= 8 theorem is an infinite structural restriction moving the minimum prime-factor count of any example, scored bound like the pre-snapshot omega bounds; unreviewed and doubtful because the enumeration cannot be replayed. Its acknowledgement says the AI discovered and proved the lemmas and ran the computations, with humans directing and reviewing: generated. Zemann's 2023 claim is knocked down by the specific unanswered coverage gap. The unread 2025 nonexistence note is set aside as not credible. Odd-square (Cattaneo) and special-form nonexistence (Cohen FQ) are cases of the existence question.
doubts: The 2608 AI quote came via a summarising fetch, not raw PDF. Whether omega restrictions count as 'bound' or as not touching an existence question was a close call.
